places.name: Pen y Fan Summit
places.ai_summary: The highest peak in South Wales, Pen y Fan offers breathtaking views of the Brecon Beacons National Park. A popular hiking destination, it features well-maintained trails and stunning vistas of rolling hills and valleys.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in clear weather for optimal views.

places.place_tip: Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring layers as the weather can change quickly at the summit.
places.address: Brecon Beacons National Park, LD3 8NL, United Kingdom

places.name: Brecon Cathedral
places.ai_summary: A historic cathedral dating back to the 11th century, featuring stunning stained glass windows, a peaceful cloister garden, and a rich history. The cathedral is a spiritual and cultural hub in the heart of Brecon.

opening_hours.notes: Check for special services and events.

places.place_tip: Visit the Heritage Centre to learn about the cathedral's history and its role in the community.
places.address: Cathedral Close, Brecon LD3 9DP, United Kingdom

places.name: Brecon Canal Basin
places.ai_summary: A picturesque starting point for exploring the Monmouthshire and Brecon Canal. The basin features colorful narrowboats, waterside cafes, and opportunities for boat hire and leisurely walks along the towpath.

opening_hours.notes: Boat hire available during daylight hours.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a sunset stroll along the towpath for a peaceful end to your day.
places.address: Canal Rd, Brecon LD3 7EW, United Kingdom

places.name: Four Waterfalls Walk
places.ai_summary: A stunning circular walk in the Brecon Beacons National Park, taking in four spectacular waterfalls: Sgwd Clun-gwyn, Sgwd y Pannwr, Sgwd yr Eira, and Sgwd Isaf Clun-gwyn. The trail offers breathtaking scenery and a chance to experience the park's natural beauty up close.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited after rainfall for maximum waterfall flow.

places.place_tip: Bring waterproof clothing and sturdy shoes, and be prepared for a moderate hike.
places.address: Waterfall Country, Brecon Beacons National Park, LD3 8NL, United Kingdom

attribution.author: Hogyncymru
attribution.description: Pronunciation of the Welsh name 'Bannau Brycheiniog', (Brecon Beacons in English).

places.name: Sgwd yr Eira Waterfall
places.ai_summary: A stunning waterfall located on the Four Waterfalls Walk, Sgwd yr Eira is unique for the ability to walk behind the falling water. This natural wonder is a must-see for visitors to the Brecon Beacons.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited after rainfall for maximum waterfall flow.

places.place_tip: Wear waterproof clothing and be prepared to get wet if you walk behind the waterfall.
places.address: Waterfall Country, Brecon Beacons National Park, LD3 8NL, United Kingdom

places.name: National Showcaves Centre for Wales
places.ai_summary: A fascinating attraction featuring impressive showcaves, including the largest cave in the UK, and an extensive collection of minerals and fossils. The centre offers guided tours and educational exhibits about geology and cave ecology.

opening_hours.notes: Advance booking recommended for cave tours.

places.place_tip: Wear warm clothing as caves can be cold, and bring a camera to capture the stunning formations.
places.address: The National Showcaves Centre for Wales, Abercrave, Swansea, SA9 1GJ, United Kingdom

places.name: Henrhyd Falls
places.ai_summary: The highest waterfall in South Wales, Henrhyd Falls is a spectacular sight, especially after heavy rain. The falls are located in a beautiful wooded area, with a short walk from the nearest car park.

opening_hours.notes: Best viewed after rainfall.

places.place_tip: Take the short walk from the car park to the falls for the best views.
places.address: Henrhyd Falls, Craig-yr-Nos, Swansea, SA9 1GJ, United Kingdom

places.name: Craig-y-Nos Country Park
places.ai_summary: A beautiful country park featuring scenic walks, picnic areas, and the historic Craig-y-Nos Castle. The park is set in the stunning Brecon Beacons National Park and offers a variety of outdoor activities.

opening_hours.notes: Castle open for tours on weekends and bank holidays.

places.place_tip: Explore the castle ruins and enjoy a picnic in the park.
places.address: Craig-y-Nos Country Park, Penycae, Swansea, SA9 1GL, United Kingdom

places.name: Brecon Mountain Railway
places.ai_summary: A scenic railway offering breathtaking views of the Brecon Beacons. The steam train journey takes you through beautiful landscapes, including mountains, forests, and rivers.

opening_hours.notes: Advance booking recommended, especially in peak season.

places.place_tip: Sit on the left side of the train for the best views.
places.address: Brecon Mountain Railway, Pant, Merthyr Tydfil, CF48 2DG, United Kingdom

places.name: Tretower Court & Castle
places.ai_summary: A historic site featuring the ruins of a 12th-century castle and a beautifully preserved medieval court. Tretower Court offers a glimpse into the life of the Welsh nobility in the Middle Ages.

opening_hours.notes: Check for guided tour availability.

places.place_tip: Explore the castle ruins and enjoy the views from the tower.
places.address: Tretower, Crickhowell, NP8 1RD, United Kingdom

places.name: Llangorse Lake
places.ai_summary: The largest natural lake in south Wales, Llangorse Lake is a popular spot for fishing, sailing, and birdwatching. The lake is surrounded by beautiful countryside and offers a range of outdoor activities.

opening_hours.notes: Fishing permits required for anglers.

places.place_tip: Visit the lakeside café for refreshments and enjoy the views across the water.
places.address: Llangorse Lake, Llangorse, Brecon, LD3 7TR, United Kingdom

places.name: Table Mountain (Crickhowell)
places.ai_summary: A prominent mountain overlooking the town of Crickhowell, Table Mountain is known for its flat top and offers stunning views of the Usk Valley and the Black Mountains. It's a popular spot for walking and picnicking.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in good weather for panoramic views.

places.place_tip: Bring a picnic and enjoy the views from the top of the mountain.
places.address: Table Mountain, Crickhowell, NP8 1LP, United Kingdom

attribution.title: Gelli-Felen halt
attribution.author: Gareth James
attribution.description:
Gelli-Felen halt
The former halt on the Merthyr, Tredegar and Abergavenny Railway. Both platform shelters survive; attached to each was a short, wooden platform, some of the timbers of which are still in situ.

National Cycle Network route 46 passes to the left.

places.name: Black Mountain Pass Drive
places.ai_summary: A scenic drive through the Brecon Beacons, the Black Mountain Pass offers stunning views of the mountains, valleys, and lakes. The route is popular with drivers, cyclists, and photographers.

opening_hours.notes: Drive carefully and be aware of cyclists and pedestrians.

places.place_tip: Stop at the viewpoints along the way for stunning photos of the landscape.
places.address: Black Mountain Pass, Brecon Beacons, LD3 8NL, United Kingdom

places.name: Talgarth Mill
places.ai_summary: A restored 19th-century watermill, Talgarth Mill offers a glimpse into the region's industrial heritage. Visitors can explore the mill, learn about its history, and enjoy the surrounding gardens and walks.

opening_hours.notes: Check for special events and milling demonstrations.

places.place_tip: Explore the mill and enjoy a walk along the River Enig.
places.address: Talgarth Mill, Talgarth, Brecon, LD3 0BW, United Kingdom

places.name: Waterfall Country (Pontneddfechan)
places.ai_summary: A stunning area in the Brecon Beacons known for its beautiful waterfalls and lush vegetation. It's a popular spot for walking, photography, and enjoying the natural beauty of Wales.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited after rainfall for maximum waterfall flow.

places.place_tip: Bring waterproof clothing and sturdy shoes, and be prepared for a moderate hike.
places.address: Waterfall Country, Pontneddfechan, Neath, SA11 5US, United Kingdom

places.name: Garwnant Visitor Centre
places.ai_summary: A popular visitor centre in the Brecon Beacons, offering information, refreshments, and access to a variety of walking and cycling trails. The centre is a great starting point for exploring the national park.

opening_hours.notes: Check for seasonal variations in opening hours.

places.place_tip: Try the homemade cakes at the visitor centre café.
places.address: Garwnant Visitor Centre, Merthyr Tydfil, CF48 2HT, United Kingdom

places.name: Afan Forest Park (edge)
places.ai_summary: The edge of Afan Forest Park offers stunning views of the forested valleys and mountains of the Brecon Beacons. It's a great spot for walking, cycling, and enjoying the natural beauty of the area.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in good weather for panoramic views.

places.place_tip: Bring binoculars for birdwatching and a camera for the stunning views.
places.address: Afan Forest Park, Port Talbot, SA13 3HG, United Kingdom

places.name: Sugar Loaf (near Abergavenny)
places.ai_summary: A prominent hill near Abergavenny, Sugar Loaf is popular for its distinctive shape and offers stunning views of the surrounding countryside. It's a great spot for walking and enjoying the outdoors.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in good weather for panoramic views.

places.place_tip: Wear sturdy shoes and bring water and snacks for your walk.
places.address: Sugar Loaf, Abergavenny, NP7 9HT, United Kingdom

places.name: Hay-on-Wye Bookshops (edge)
places.ai_summary: The edge of Hay-on-Wye is famous for its numerous second-hand bookshops, earning the town the title 'The Town of Books'. It's a paradise for book lovers and offers a unique shopping experience.

opening_hours.notes: Check individual shops for specific opening hours.

places.place_tip: Explore the backstreets for hidden gem bookshops and enjoy a coffee in a local café.

places.name: Brecon Town Centre
places.ai_summary: The historic town centre of Brecon features a mix of independent shops, cafes, and cultural attractions. It's a great place to explore on foot and soak up the local atmosphere.

opening_hours.notes: Check individual shops and attractions for specific opening hours.

places.place_tip: Visit the Brecon Museum and enjoy a walk along the River Usk.
places.address: Brecon, LD3 7AL, United Kingdom
